skill.name: angular-developer
skill.description: Builds and modernizes Angular applications using guidance for signals, forms, routing, dependency injection, accessibility, styling, testing, SSR, and CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Create maintainable Angular features with version-aware architecture and framework best practices.
skill.author: angular

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are lexical false positives from Markdown, CSS, Angular APIs, and fixed local imports. Six findings remain confirmed because the skill mandates local CLI execution or unpinned npx downloads. The MCP setup adds a high-confidence supply-chain risk by auto-running an unversioned package.

remediation.issue: MCP examples execute an unversioned package with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin @angular/cli to a reviewed version, remove -y, and require user approval before installing or starting the MCP server.

remediation.issue: The workflow mandates ng build in any current Angular workspace.
remediation.suggestion: Request approval and inspect configured builders before running builds, especially in newly opened or untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: Project names and requested versions are inserted into documented commands.
remediation.suggestion: Validate values against Angular CLI formats and pass them as separate process arguments without shell interpolation.

content.value_statement: Angular projects require version-aware patterns across components, state, forms, routing, testing, and tooling. This skill applies focused Angular guidance and verifies generated work.
actual_capabilities: Creates Angular projects and features with Angular CLI workflows.
Designs standalone components, inputs, outputs, host bindings, and accessible ARIA interactions.
Implements signals, linked state, effects, resources, and HTTP data access.
Selects signal, reactive, or template-driven form patterns for the project version.
Guides routing, dependency injection, SSR, styling, animations, and environment configuration.
Produces unit, harness, router, and end-to-end testing guidance.
limitations: Guidance depends on the Angular version and the existing workspace configuration.
External APIs, backend contracts, and product requirements must be supplied by the user.
Build success does not replace browser, accessibility, security, or production testing.
Some modern APIs, including Signal Forms, require recent Angular releases.

use_cases.title: Implement a Product Feature
use_cases.description: Create a maintainable Angular feature with components, state, forms, routing, data access, and focused tests.

use_cases.title: Modernize an Angular Workspace
use_cases.description: Review older patterns and plan version-compatible migrations toward signals, standalone APIs, and current naming conventions.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Quality Coverage
use_cases.description: Design accessible interactions and reliable unit, harness, router, and end-to-end tests for existing features.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Angular application named [name] for [purpose]. Use my installed Angular version and include routing, styling, and one tested feature.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a new Angular project with sensible defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement [feature] in this Angular workspace. Follow existing conventions and include components, typed data access, loading states, errors, and focused tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Add a complete feature to an existing application.

prompt_templates.title: Modernize Existing Code
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [area] for outdated Angular patterns. Propose a version-compatible migration to signals and standalone APIs, then implement changes with regression tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an established Angular codebase incrementally.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Application Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design the architecture for [system]. Address routing, state ownership, dependency injection, SSR, accessibility, security boundaries, testing, and staged migration constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a complex Angular application or major redesign.

output_examples.input: Create a customer search feature with server results, loading feedback, and tests.
output: A standalone feature structure aligned with the current workspace.
Signal-based query and result state with typed HTTP access.
Loading, empty, error, and accessible interaction behavior.
Focused service, component, and routing test coverage.

output_examples.input: Review this Angular application before migrating from version 18.
output: A version and dependency compatibility assessment.
Prioritized migration stages with affected framework APIs.
Risks for forms, routing, rendering, and third-party libraries.
Verification steps for builds, tests, accessibility, and runtime behavior.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for a protected checkout route with async data.
output: Router harness coverage for allowed, denied, loading, and failed navigation.
Component checks for accessible status and error feedback.

best_practices: Confirm the workspace Angular version before selecting APIs or migration steps.
Match existing architecture and naming conventions unless a migration is explicitly requested.
Verify generated changes with focused tests, a build, and relevant accessibility checks.
anti_patterns: Do not introduce recent Angular APIs into unsupported project versions.
Do not mix form strategies or state ownership patterns without a documented reason.
Do not treat successful compilation as proof of accessible, secure, or correct behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill support existing Angular projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It reviews the current version and conventions before proposing compatible features or migrations.

faq.question: Can it create a new Angular project?
faq.answer: Yes. It can select an appropriate Angular CLI command and propose project defaults based on your requirements.

faq.question: Which form approach does it recommend?
faq.answer: It prefers Signal Forms for supported new projects and follows the established strategy in older applications.

faq.question: Does it cover testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers unit tests, component harnesses, router tests, and end-to-end testing patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance for accessible custom interactions, Angular ARIA components, focus behavior, and test coverage.

faq.question: Will it run Angular CLI commands automatically?
faq.answer: The guidance includes CLI execution. Review commands, package versions, project names, and workspace trust before allowing execution.
